get.summary: Gets a team's CITE answers for a move
get.description:
Returns what the team answered on the MSEL's CITE scoring model for one move: per scoring category,
the selected options, comments and score, plus the official and team-average submissions when the
scoring model uses them. Team-level answers only; no participant's own submission.
<para />
When there is nothing to read, the status says why: the MSEL is not pushed to CITE, the team or
the move is not in CITE, the move has not started, or CITE could not be read, with a message naming
what failed: Blueprint's CITE API URL, the identity provider, or CITE, a timeout included.
<para />
Accessible with the ViewMsels permission, or to the MSEL's Owners, Editors, Approvers and Evaluators

parameters.name: moveNumber
parameters.description: The move number. Required: without it the request is a 400 rather than move 0's answers

get.summary: Gets IEEE 2881 (LMT) metadata for an MSEL as JSON-LD
get.description:
Returns LMT (Learning Metadata) as JSON-LD conforming to IEEE 2881 schema.
Accessible to any signed-in caller, to enable catalog discovery by LMS systems,
PCTE registries, and other TLA components, and only for a published MSEL: a template
with the Approved status. Any other MSEL is a 404. The JSON-LD includes:
- Exercise name, description, objectives
- Competencies assessed (lrmi:assesses from MselCompetency associations)
- Educational metadata (difficulty, purpose, mode, keywords)
- Prerequisites (if configured)
            
Any LMS that supports LTI 1.3 Deep Linking or Content-Item can consume this
metadata to auto-link competencies, tags, and prerequisites when importing
the exercise.

post.summary: Copies a Msel's Caster directory into the Msel
post.description:
Exports the Msel's linked Caster directory, and the directories above it, as the caller, and stores the
copy in place of any the Msel had. The caller must be able to view the directory and its project in
Caster. Open to EditMsels, the Msel's owner and its editors. Not while the Msel is pushed.

delete.summary: Deletes the copy of its Caster directory a Msel carries
delete.description: Deletes the Msel's copy. A Msel that links a Caster directory takes a new copy on its next JSON download.

post.summary: Imports a Msel's copy of a Caster directory into Caster
post.description:
Creates a new Caster project, as the caller, from the copy the Msel carries, and links the Msel to the
directory it creates. The caller needs Caster's Create Projects permission. Pushing a Msel that has a copy
and no directory does the same, as the pusher. A template's launches need a directory, so a template with
only a copy is imported here first. Not while the Msel is pushed, nor while it has a directory.

get.summary: Gets the variables a Msel's teams can be mapped to in its Caster topology
get.description:
Returns the team variables of the Msel's linked Caster directory, read from Caster as the caller, or, for
a Msel with no directory, of the copy it carries. Empty when it has neither.

post.summary: Imports a mappings file onto a release
post.description:
The file is read as the release's framework defines its mappings. Rows are aggregated to one per (source
id, target technique), weighted by distinct paths; a pair whose target is not a technique of this release
is skipped and counted. Importing again replaces the release's mappings. Refused with a 400 when the
release's framework defines no mappings or the file is not of their format.

post.description:
The file is read as the technique framework whose match conditions it meets; a 400 when none does or more
than one does. Give the framework to choose one. The version is read from the file; give one only for a
file that does not name it.

parameters.name: techniqueFrameworkId
parameters.description: The framework to read the file as, if more than one matches

projectName.description: The Caster project the directory was exported from; an import creates a project by this name.

directories.description: From the project's root directory down to the exported directory, which is last.

entries.description: The exported directory's contents as Caster exported them, by their paths in the export.

contentsIncluded.description: Whether file contents are included; only those who may change the copy read them.

warnings.description: What the copy could not carry, when it was just taken from Caster.

MselCasterExport.description:
The copy of a Caster directory a MSEL carries, read only. A MSEL that links a Caster directory refreshes
it on every JSON download; a push to a Caster without the directory imports it as a new project.

files.description: A directory above the exported one: its own shared files. The exported directory's are in Entries.

path.description: The path in the export, relative to the exported directory.

workspace.description: The workspace the file belongs to, or null for a directory's shared file.

warnings.description: What the import changed to fit Caster, such as a directory name Caster no longer takes.

MselCasterImportResult.description: The Caster directory an import of a MSEL's Caster copy created, and what Caster did not import.

techniqueReleaseId.description:
The defensive release the mappings come from: the one the MSEL is pinned to, else the newest with mappings.
Null when none has mappings.

hasMappings.description: True when that release has mappings imported; false when the pinned release has none yet.

MselCountermeasures.description: The countermeasures of every attack technique in a MSEL's pool, from one defensive release.

articleMarking.description:
The banner Blueprint puts on the MSEL's Gallery articles when it pushes them, and on its pages: None (the default),
Exercise, Tlp or Classification. A value it does not know is saved as None.

articleMarkingText.description: The TLP level (CLEAR, GREEN, AMBER, AMBER+STRICT, RED), or the classification banner's text, up to 120 characters

casterDirectoryId.description: The Caster directory a push deploys from, which the caller must be able to view.

hideNamesOnAssessorView.description:
Leaves out who each xAPI statement is about when the Assessor View lists them, so an assessor
rates the team's work without seeing its members' names. The MSEL's owners and anyone with
ViewMsels still see the names. The statements in the LRS are unchanged.

articleMarking.description:
The banner Blueprint puts on the MSEL's Gallery articles when it pushes them, and on its pages: None (the default),
Exercise, Tlp or Classification. A value it does not know is saved as None.

articleMarkingText.description: The TLP level (CLEAR, GREEN, AMBER, AMBER+STRICT, RED), or the classification banner's text, up to 120 characters

casterDirectoryId.description: The Caster directory a push deploys from, which the caller must be able to view.

hideNamesOnAssessorView.description:
Leaves out who each xAPI statement is about when the Assessor View lists them, so an assessor
rates the team's work without seeing its members' names. The MSEL's owners and anyone with
ViewMsels still see the names. The statements in the LRS are unchanged.

step.description: The import step that failed, e.g. "citeScoringModel" or "citeTeamTypes".

field.description: The MSEL field concerned, e.g. "name" or "citeScoringModel".

changes.description: Values the import changed or dropped, and settings the importer should check before pushing.

failures.description: Steps that could not run, e.g. CITE was unreachable. The MSEL was still imported.

MselImportResult.description:
What a JSON MSEL import did. The import never stops for a missing CITE scoring model,
an unknown team type or an unreachable CITE, so this is how the importer finds out
what was changed or skipped instead of discovering it at push time.

steamfitterScenarioStatus.description: The Steamfitter scenario's status - Ready until it is started, then Active, then Ended.

MselIntegrationNames.description: The display names of the things a MSEL is integrated with.

articleMarking.description:
The MSEL's marking and name, so a reader of the page can draw its banner without reading the MSEL, which a
page reader may not be allowed to; null when the MSEL is not loaded.

moveNumberFirstDisplay.description: The first move whose score sheet shows the category, when the model displays by move number.

options.description: In display order. A replace numbers them in the order they are sent.

categories.description: In display order. A replace numbers them in the order they are sent.

MselScoringModel.description:
The CITE scoring model a MSEL authors itself, with CITE's ScoringModel fields. Pushing the MSEL creates it
in CITE for the MSEL's evaluation.

MselScoringModelLink.description: The CITE scoring model a MSEL links, or none.

inheritedFrom.description: The parent technique's id when some of these are inherited from it, from a release with no mappings of the technique's own; else null.

MselTechniqueCountermeasures.description: The countermeasures of one pooled attack technique, ranked by weight.

dropped.description: The technique ids the new release no longer has, revoked or deprecated.

MselTechniqueUpgrade.description: What moving a MSEL's technique pool to another release kept and dropped.

mselId.description: The MSEL the application belongs to, or null for a template.

scenarioEventId.description: On an edit, a cell is written only when this names the event being edited.

ScenarioEventCell.description: One cell of a Scenario Event in a create or edit request: the Data Field it is for and its value.

dataValues.description: The event's cells. Only cells for the MSEL's own Data Fields are written.
The event's cells. Only cells for the MSEL's own Data Fields are written.

isScored.description:
The category has a calculation equation, so it is scored. Read only: set from the equation

before it is redacted, so callers who cannot see the equation can still tell scored categories apart.

ScoringModelPreset.description: The starting points a MSEL's own scoring model can be created from.

SteamfitterTaskFields.description: The editable fields of a Scenario Event's Steamfitter task.

isDefensive.description: Whether the technique is a defence (its release is defensive) rather than an attack.

tactics.description: The short names of the tactics the technique serves, e.g. "execution".

weaknesses.description: The ids of the weaknesses the technique exploits; empty when the framework gives none.

referenceLinks.description: The technique's links to other catalogues; empty when the framework gives none.

techniqueReleaseId.description: The defensive release the mapping belongs to.

offensiveExternalId.description: The source technique's id, whichever release of its framework the MSEL uses.

defensiveTactic.description: The tactic label the mapping is filed under, as the file gives it.

rationale.description: The most common path behind the pair, as the file words it.

weight.description: The number of distinct artifact paths that link the pair; the list is ranked by it.

inheritedFromParent.description: True when the offensive id asked for had no mappings of its own and these are its parent technique's.

TechniqueCountermeasure.description: A mapping: the source technique id and the technique of the release it maps to.

rowsRead.description: The result rows in the file, one per artifact path per queried technique.

pairsStored.description: The distinct (offensive id, defensive technique) pairs stored.

pairsSkipped.description: Pairs whose defensive class is not a defensive technique in this release, so they were left out.

offensiveTechniqueCount.description: The distinct offensive technique ids the stored pairs cover.

TechniqueCountermeasureImport.description: What importing a mappings file onto a defensive release read and kept.

domain.description: The domain its releases are filed under; unique across frameworks.

isDefensive.description: Whether its techniques are defences rather than attacks.

releaseCount.description: The releases read as this framework; read only.

TechniqueFramework.description:
A technique framework definition: how its release files are recognised and read, and how their content is
shown. An administrator creates, edits, imports and exports them; Blueprint ships none.

TechniqueLink.description: A link from a technique to the same attack in another catalogue.

techniqueFrameworkId.description: The framework the release was read as; null for a release that has none.

isDefensive.description: Whether the release's techniques are defences rather than attacks.

source.description: Who publishes the release; null when it is not known.

notice.description: The copyright and trademark notice to show with the release's content, one line per sentence group; null when it carries none.

groupLabel.description: What the release calls its groups of techniques: "Tactics" or "Categories".

countermeasureCount.description: The mappings imported onto the release.

tacticOrder.description: The framework's tactic names in the order they are shown; empty when it gives none.

weaknessUrlTemplate.description: A weakness's page, with {id} and {fullId}; null when the framework gives none.

mappingRelation.description: How the framework's mappings read, as its definition words the relation; null when the framework has no mappings to import.

mappingsDownloadUrl.description: Where the release's mappings file is downloaded from; null when the framework does not say.

techniqueFrameworkId.description: The framework the release belongs to, of the same domain and family; null for none.

source.description: Who publishes the release; blank for none.

sourceUrl.description: The publisher's website for the framework, an http or https address; blank for none.

notice.description: The copyright and trademark notice to show with the release's content, one line per sentence group; blank for none.

termsUrl.description: The publisher's terms of use, an http or https address; blank for none.

TechniqueReleaseNotice.description:
What an administrator may edit on a release: its framework and its notice fields. Nothing else about a
release changes.
